issue.title: test_chops_run_concurrently asserts a fixed 1.8-second host-speed ceiling
issue.description: PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-um.5.1.3 note #3. tests/test_axe_lumberjack_tick.py::test_chops_run_concurrently failed once in Master Gate run 33076444255: two mocked one-second chops completed in 2.0 seconds versus the test fixed elapsed < 1.8 assertion. A direct same-tree rerun passed in 3.77 seconds overall with a 1.01-second call. Current source proves concurrency only by sleeping one second in each mock and imposing that absolute wall-clock ceiling, so host scheduling pressure can fail the test without serial chop execution. Replace the machine-speed assertion with synchronization or overlap evidence that directly proves both chops run concurrently, while preserving the call-count and metrics assertions.

task_type_fields.evidence: Failed once in Master Gate run 33076444255 at 2.0 seconds against elapsed < 1.8; immediate local rerun passed with a 1.01-second call. One full-lane failure and one isolated pass on the same tree. The current fixed sleep plus elapsed ceiling measures scheduler speed as well as concurrency.

payload.description: same root cause class: a test asserting a fixed absolute wall-clock ceiling that host contention can exceed
